To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mode of interaction between a fold and a thrust fault will depend on the relative resistance of the fold and thrust to foreland translation and internal deformation and that this resistance will vary with the strength and thickness of the layers, the presence of anisotropic layering, the amount of slip that is transferred out of the fold and into the hanging wall, and the presence of imbricate faults.

(a) the mode of fold and thrust interaction depends on the relative strength of the hanging wall to the resistance to translation of the thrust system and (b) during shortening, the mode of fold-propagation folding can switch to a fault-bend mode, and the mode of fault-bend folding can switch to fault propagation.
the mode of fault-bend versus fault-propagation fold interaction is controlled by the relative strength of the thrust sheet and the overlying cover and by the strength of the layer interfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the mechanical properties and geometry of a deforming region on the structural development and strain distribution within the region.
the structural development of thrust systems in layered rock.
the development of fault-bent and fault-propagation fold-thrust structures in heterogeneous rock.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a single layer of rock containing a ramp, the mode of fold interaction depends upon the relative strength of the layering and the ramp.

the geometry, kinematics, and mechanics of fault-bend folds and fault-propagation fold systems are complex and that the interaction between folds and faults is controlled by the mechanical properties of the layers and the strength of the faults.
the mode of interaction between a propagating thrust and the hanging wall is determined by the relative resistance of the thrust system to foreland translation and internal deformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mode of fault-bend or fault-propagation folding activated in a thrust sheet will depend on the loading conditions, strength of the layers and layer interfaces, and the geometry of the ramp.
the structural development of a fold-thrust system is a complex process that depends on the mechanical properties of the rocks, their layering, and boundary conditions.
fault-bend folding and fault-propagation are not discrete modes of folding, but that both modes of deformation are activated during shortening of a thrust sheet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fault-bend folds are not the only structures produced by fault-propagation fold systems.
the mode of interaction of fold and thrust is controlled by the mechanical strength ratio of the hanging wall relative to the ramp.
a single mode of fold-thust interaction does not occur during the structural evolution of a fold-and-thrust belt, even in the simplest of models.
